ActiveInstructionOut.description:
One instruction in force, and where it came from.

The source travels to the client because the question it answers — "why does
it write like this, and where do I change it?" — is asked by a person looking
at a screen, not by the resolver.
ActiveInstructionOut.title: ActiveInstructionOut

ActorAction.description: A human action. The actor is mandatory: an anonymous decision is unreviewable.
ActorAction.title: ActorAction

ActorType.description:
What kind of thing acted: who emitted an event or made a decision.

``POLICY`` is not a person — it is a versioned rule set, which is why a
policy decision must also carry a ``policy_version``.
ActorType.title: ActorType

AnswerGap.description: One answer to one surfaced question.
AnswerGap.title: AnswerGap

AnswerResponse.description:
What the author did with a question (phase 06 §3).

All six are answers in the sense that matters: each one tells the pipeline
something it did not know, and each is recorded. They differ in two ways that
the code depends on — whether the question is closed, and whether the text may
be sent to a model.

``DEFERRED`` is the only one that leaves the question pending: postponing is
not resolving, and marking it closed would erase the record that the author
meant to come back. ``CONFIDENTIAL`` is the only one whose text is deliberately
withheld from the provider while still being kept locally — it is an answer to
the pipeline and a refusal to the model at the same time.
AnswerResponse.title: AnswerResponse

ApproveSuggestion.description: Making an inferred rule permanent, and naming the version it becomes.
ApproveSuggestion.title: ApproveSuggestion

ArticleDepth.description:
How deep the finished article goes, declared per project.

A project constraint rather than a stage decision: it bounds scope for every
stage at once (extraction's token budget, the architecture's article count,
the brief's length), and letting each stage infer it would let them disagree.
ArticleDepth.title: ArticleDepth

CommandResponse.description: The answer to every command: position, affordances, and any queued work.
CommandResponse.title: CommandResponse

CreateProject.description:
Open a project. The constraints are required, not defaulted.

A project's audience, platform and permitted providers decide what may be
written and who may see the material; guessing them would mean guessing
whether an external provider is allowed to read the source.
CreateProject.title: CreateProject

EditorialConstraints.description:
The bounds a project publishes under (phase 06 §1).

A *value*, not a record: :class:`ProjectConstraints` is the versioned row that
holds one of these. Splitting them is what lets ingestion ask "are these the
constraints already in force?" by comparing values, and version them only when
the answer is no.

``allowed_providers`` is an allow-list. A project that has not named a
provider has not consented to it seeing the material, so the default is that
nothing external may — local-first by default (plan/00), enforced end to end
in phase 13.
EditorialConstraints.title: EditorialConstraints

EffectiveVoice.description: The resolved voice, and the profiles it was resolved from.
EffectiveVoice.title: EffectiveVoice

ExecutionComparison.description: Two executions, side by side. Phase 12 says what the difference means.
ExecutionComparison.title: ExecutionComparison

ExecutionStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a pipeline run or a stage execution.

``FAILED`` and ``CANCELLED`` are deliberately distinct: one is the system
giving up, the other a human stopping the work. Both keep their partial
trace (plan/03 → *Failure handling*, partial data preserved).
ExecutionStatus.title: ExecutionStatus

ExecutionSummary.description: One stage execution, as a client sees it.
ExecutionSummary.title: ExecutionSummary

FindingStatus.description:
What the author decided about one review finding (phase 07 §8).

Five states because a criticism has five fates, and collapsing any two of them
loses something the next round needs. ``REJECTED`` is the author disagreeing;
``SUPPRESSED`` is the *system* holding back a finding the author already
dismissed, raised again with nothing new behind it. Neither deletes anything:
plan/07 requires resolved criticism to stay visible, so a dismissed finding is
kept with the reason it was dismissed for.
FindingStatus.title: FindingStatus

ImportSource.description: Add one piece of source material to a project.
ImportSource.title: ImportSource

InstructionStrength.description:
How firmly an instruction binds (plan/10 → Instruction strength model).

Declared in descending order of force, and the order is meaningful: a
resolver comparing two instructions for the same thing takes the stronger.

- ``HARD_RULE`` — rarely violated, and *checked*. This is the only strength
  the system verifies mechanically, which is why a hard rule has to name
  something findable in the finished text.
- ``STRONG_PREFERENCE`` — normally followed; a justified exception is
  allowed, and the model is told so rather than being left to guess whether
  it may ever deviate.
- ``TENDENCY`` — the usual style, offered as such. Explicitly *not* a
  template: plan/10's named risk is homogenisation, and a tendency applied
  as a mandate is how that happens.
InstructionStrength.title: InstructionStrength

InvocationOutcome.description:
How a single model invocation ended.

``INVALID_JSON`` and ``INVALID_SCHEMA`` are separate because a response can
be useful yet unparseable, or parseable yet non-conforming; both are
preserved alongside their repaired successor rather than discarded.
InvocationOutcome.title: InvocationOutcome

Job.description: One unit of queued work, as stored and as reported.
Job.title: Job

JobStatus.description:
Where a queued unit of work has got to.

``SUPERSEDED`` is the member that earns this enum its own existence: a job
replaced by a newer command is neither cancelled (nobody stopped it) nor
failed (nothing went wrong). It is work the system decided not to do, and
saying so is the difference between a queue that can be audited and one that
silently drops requests.
JobStatus.title: JobStatus

ModelInvocationOut.description:
One model call, including the attempts that failed.

The failed ones are published, not filtered: a client showing only accepted
calls would under-report exactly the runs that cost the most.
ModelInvocationOut.title: ModelInvocationOut

RejectSuggestion.description: Declining an inferred rule, with the reason kept.
RejectSuggestion.title: RejectSuggestion

SourceFormat.description:
How a source document arrived, which decides how it is segmented.

From *Editorial workflow §1 Source ingestion*: Markdown, plain text and pasted
notes are the three supported inputs. The distinction is kept after parsing
because it explains the segmentation: a heading in Markdown is a structural
fact, whereas the same line in pasted notes is just a line.
SourceFormat.title: SourceFormat

TraceEventOut.description: One event in a run's timeline.
TraceEventOut.title: TraceEventOut

UpdateArchitecture.description: An author's edits to a proposed architecture.
UpdateArchitecture.title: UpdateArchitecture

VoiceCategory.description:
What an instruction is about (plan/10 → VoiceProfile structure).

Five, because that is how a person reads and edits a profile: the categories
are the sections of the document, not an internal taxonomy. ``PROHIBITED_
PATTERNS`` is the one that is not a facet of style but a list of things never
to write, and it earns its own category because it is the one people add to
most often — usually right after seeing the pattern in their own draft.
VoiceCategory.title: VoiceCategory

VoiceInstruction.description:
One thing the author's prose does, or never does.

``id`` is stable across versions and scopes, and that is its whole purpose:
it is how an article override replaces the project's version of the same
instruction rather than sitting beside it. Ids are chosen by whoever writes
the instruction — ``no-em-dash``, ``open-concrete`` — because a generated id
could not be matched across two profiles written months apart.

``prohibits`` holds literal strings that must not appear in finished prose.
Literals rather than patterns on purpose: a regular expression in a voice
profile is a thing the author cannot read, and every rule this has been
needed for so far — an em dash, a banned product name, a hype word — is a
literal.
VoiceInstruction.title: VoiceInstruction

VoiceProfileDocument.description:
A named, versioned set of instructions at one scope.

Replaces the placeholder phase 07 shipped with. The two fields it kept —
``name`` and ``version`` — are the ones already written into article records,
so an article drafted before this phase still names something meaningful.
VoiceProfileDocument.title: VoiceProfileDocument

VoiceProfileSummary.description: One stored profile version, as a client lists them.
VoiceProfileSummary.title: VoiceProfileSummary

VoiceScope.description:
Where a profile applies (plan/10 → voice hierarchy).

Ordered widest to narrowest, which is also precedence order: an article
override beats a project profile beats the author's global one. The narrower
scope wins because it is the more deliberate act — a person who set something
for one article meant it for that article.
VoiceScope.title: VoiceScope

VoiceSuggestionOut.description: An inferred rule awaiting an answer, with the edits behind it.
VoiceSuggestionOut.title: VoiceSuggestionOut

WorkflowState.description:
Where a pipeline run currently sits.

The order mirrors the editorial pipeline: source → architecture → brief →
draft → review → voice → score → validate → approve, with the three endings
last. Names ending in ``_REQUIRED`` are the human-pause states — the engine
parks there until a person acts (see
:func:`~groundscribe.workflow.transitions.human_pause_states`).
WorkflowState.title: WorkflowState

info.description: A local-first, inspectable editorial workflow. Every command returns where the run now is and what may be done to it next; work that calls a model is queued for a worker rather than done in the request.
info.title: groundscribe

post.description: The author publishes the validated article.
Accept the brief, which is what opens drafting.
Queue the brief this article will be drafted against.
Queue the first draft.
Accept an article the score refused, on a person's explicit say-so.
Queue a substantive review of the current version.
Queue the plan a rewrite will be bound by.
Authorise the rewrite the plan describes.
Queue the rewrite.
Queue the scoring pass, which is also what routes a failure.
Run final validation here and now: it calls no model (plan/08).
Queue the voice pass.

get.description:
Two executions side by side. Declared before ``/executions/{id}`` so the
literal path is matched first rather than read as an execution called
"compare".
One stage execution, with how it ended.
The execution's timeline, in the order it was recorded.

schema.title: Response Read Execution Events Executions  Execution Id  Events Get

post.description: Branch a new execution from an existing one.

get.description: Every model call the execution made, failed attempts included.

schema.title: Response Read Execution Invocations Executions  Execution Id  Invocations Get

post.description: Re-run a stage as a new execution. The original is never touched.
Open an experiment record; phase 12 fills in what it means.

get.description: One job, for a client that would rather poll than stream.

Stream a job's progress until it finishes.

``after`` is a sequence number rather than a count, so a client that
reconnects resumes from what it saw instead of replaying the run — the same
contract as SSE's ``Last-Event-ID``, which phase 03's stored event ordering
already supports.

post.description: Open a project, its bounds, its run and its position.

get.description: Where the run is and what may be done to it, changing nothing.

post.description: Queue a proposal of the article or series the source supports.

put.description:
Commit an author's edits as a new version.

``version`` addresses the architecture the author was looking at. The service
edits the version currently in force; a mismatch is a conflict the engine's
lineage guard raises, which is the check that actually matters.

post.description: Lock the architecture, and open an article for each approved concept.
Stop the run. Available in every non-terminal state, so none is a trap.
Record an answer and rebuild the source model from it.
Queue the source-model build, and the gap analysis that follows it.
Store one piece of source material. No model is involved, so no job.

get.description: The voice in force here, and where each instruction came from.
Every version this author has saved, in force or superseded.

schema.title: Response List Voice Profiles Voice Profiles Get

post.description:
Put a profile version in force at its scope.

The body is the profile *document* itself rather than an API-shaped wrapper.
It is what the author edits and what the voice pass consumes, and a second
shape in between would be a place for the two to disagree — including about
whether a hard rule names anything checkable, which the document validates
and a wrapper would have to remember to.

get.description: Inferred rules still waiting for an answer. Listing applies nothing.

schema.title: Response List Voice Suggestions Voice Suggestions Get

post.description: Make an inferred rule permanent. The only endpoint that changes a voice.
Record that the author said no, and why.
